title: Learning Global Representation from Queries for Vectorized HD Map Construction
claim: Conventional query-based pipelines yield locally inconsistent predictions; injecting a global embedding into queries yields predictions better aligned with global structure.
layout: 3 panels: inputs left, two stacked pipelines right; red ellipses highlight differences
description: The figure has three parts. Panel (a), at left, shows a mosaic of six on-vehicle camera photos labeled 'On-vehicle Images', beside a vectorized ground-truth HD map with red and yellow dotted lines; red ellipses mark one region. A vertical divider separates it from the right side. Panel (b), top right, shows a conventional DETR-like pipeline: light-blue query squares Q1 go through gray decoder-layer bars to produce query set Qi, then a prediction map whose red-circled region looks distorted. Panel (c), bottom right, repeats the flow with a 'Map Global Embedding' orange square feeding the decoder. The output queries are half orange and half blue. The resulting prediction is circled in red and better matches the ground truth.
caption: (a) Multi-view images from on-board sensors. (b) A conventional DETR-like HD map construction pipeline. (c) Our proposed global representation learning of queries for the map construction task significantly improves query distribution from the initial to the final decoder layers. This improvement leads to smoother and more consistent curvature changes in instances, ensuring better alignment with the global structure. $Q_{i}$ represents the query set from the $i$-th decoding layer. The red box marks a region where query distribution improves significantly.
abstract: The online construction of vectorized high-definition (HD) maps is a cornerstone of modern autonomous driving systems. State-of-the-art approaches, particularly those based on the DETR framework, formulate this as an instance detection problem. However, their reliance on independent, learnable object queries results in a predominantly local query perspective, neglecting the inherent global representation within HD maps. In this work, we propose \textbf{MapGR} (\textbf{G}lobal \textbf{R}epresentation learning for HD \textbf{Map} construction), an architecture designed to learn and utilize a global representations from queries. Our method introduces two synergistic modules: a Global Representation Learning (GRL) module, which encourages the distribution of all queries to better align with the global map through a carefully designed holistic segmentation task, and a Global Representation Guidance (GRG) module, which endows each individual query with explicit, global-level contextual information to facilitate its optimization. Evaluations on the nuScenes and Argoverse2 datasets validate the efficacy of our approach, demonstrating substantial improvements in mean Average Precision (mAP) compared to leading baselines.
